newApp: It runs under Docker Compose: a compose.yaml at the repo root declares every service the app needs (the app built from its own Dockerfile, and any database, cache or worker it uses), so that `docker compose up` starts it with no other step.
Data lives in named volumes, not in bind mounts of host folders; ports and settings come from environment variables with working defaults, documented in a .env.example.
The README says how to start, stop and reset it with Docker Compose.

Check it before reporting: `docker compose config` and `docker compose build` pass, and the app answers once `docker compose up -d` has started it; stop it again afterwards (`docker compose down`). From this container, Docker sees /app as the host's ~/dev: run compose with `--project-directory /home/dremsis/dev/<repo>` when a relative path matters.
